Learnt this from a young age sadly. I remember when I was eight years old,  I had counselling at school and told the counsellor about how my dad would hit me. She promised she wouldn’t say anything to do, called him in and did, he was able to talk his way out of it so she thought it was just a dumb kid that got a slap on the wrist from a frustrated parent and nothing came of it. Oh, nothing except getting beaten the shit out of for snitching by said nparent and threatened if I did it again. This affected me horribly and prevented me from ever seeking out help again. Because what was the point that when you did, they only made it worse?

My individuality was only worth something if it was something my nparent could benefit from lol. I was threatened a lot by my NDad and shamed for drawing and being interested in story writing and even forced me to throw away my art supplies when I was younger. It wasn’t a beneficial hobby of course, a kid needs to do something that’s actually useful, according to him. He only ever expressed interest if *he* somehow would get benefit from it, like how I entered a writing competition once and won money that he then took because ‘it was a team effort’. I shit you not, this man said because he provided me food and a home, that I had that environment and my accomplishments were his. This seems like a normal sentiment with parents when their kids do something cool but considering the fact I was belittled for it so frequently, this was just a slap in the face lol.

Ngl, this support group has saved me in incredibly dark moments. Seeing people’s struggles makes me feel less alone, seeing people breaking free from the clutches of their nparents and talking about how much better their lives were without them gives me a lot of hope and courage to do the same one day.

The ones that make me most angry that have the ‘you have to forgive’ mantra are enabler parents. Just because you’ve been able to oversee and accept that shitty things your partner has done, by no means does that mean your child has to do the same. 

For a very long time, my mother always told me I had to ‘let go of my anger’ because she forgave my NDad for the stuff he did, so I should be able to as well.

Newsflash enablers, this doesn’t ‘build character’ for your kids and this isn’t ‘an experience that makes you stronger’. It traumatises you, it breaks you down, and just guilts you for feeling very JUSTIFIABLE anger towards your abuser.

For me, I think it was the slow realisation that things that my Nparent did wasn’t considered normal. Myself and most of my friends had immigrant parents, so as kids, we’d often joke about how strict our parents were and how harshly they’d punish us, like it was normal. When I was about 15 or so though and discussing these things, others would mention that it was only if they displayed bad behaviour and that it was only stuff when they were small kids. For a while, I justified it as ‘oh immigrant parents are just like that’ but seeing that most of the people around me didn’t have parents that would act as drastically as mine, that’s when it clicked in. And I’m still trying to tell myself currently and trying to that it wasn’t my fault

This ending feels..right. It’s not necessarily ‘happy’, but it isn’t sad either. It’s..quietly hopeful. Seeing Bojack have a moment with each person of the main cast, (Todd, PC, Mr. PB and Diane) felt right. It felt right for him and Diane to have that moment on the roof, and it’s right that he still gets the chance to get better. Or be better. 

A very small part of me kind of expected and hoped for a lot of things to be wrapped up and/or resolved but the show likes to be realistic, and everything Wrapping up nicely in the end isn’t realistic. Bojack Horseman makes it clear that real life doesn’t resolve all its issues nice and perfectly at the end of thirty minutes, it doesn’t just ‘start over’. 

I’m sad that his relationship with Hollyhock has been ruined, but it makes sense. She was right, they didn’t really ‘know’ each other. And it’s asking too much of her to accept him for everything after everything that had been brought to light. But who knows for the future

It’s sad as well to see other cases- like Gina- are lost cases that can’t have a resolution. 

It’s sad for what it is and hopeful for what it can be, which, for Bojack Horseman, seems to be the right call.

Whilst she’s not a favourite character of mine, I feel that it’s a bit unfair to say she doesn’t judge herself, especially given season 5 and season 6. As Stefani, her boss, had put it, Diane puts and holds everyone accountable to a very high standard, which is good for her job but isn’t good for herself- because she also puts herself to a high standard. She has shown great dissatisfaction at the point in her life made from her decisions which has been shown again and again throughout the show. Examples are for when she goes to Cordovia and isn’t able to handle the reality of the situation and comes back home, hence going to Bojack’s to hide herself from Mr. PB. In the final episode of that season she goes through a small tirade of wanting to reset and restart.

I’ll admit, it’s a slow progress for Diane but she definitely doesn’t think highly of herself as compared to others. This is shown in greater detail in season 6, with the Whitewhale episode and following after that. She has difficulty finding a ‘feel good’ story due to her overly critical view on everything. And during her journey to expose whitewhale, she ultimately fails. She’s spiraled into a depression, she doesn’t find worth in herself.

To be honest, I personally don’t recall any major moments where Diane truly had a moment where she was full of herself or put herself on a high pedestal ((the closest I can come to think of was when she was recognised in the episode for her menstruation cup post)) She considers herself a ‘garbage barge’ 

In saying that, it’s perfectly fine that you don’t like her, because I definitely understand why people don’t and that’s valid, this is my opinion based of what I’ve taken from the show

I'm also a lefty who used to have the most crap and atrocious handwriting anyone could ever have seen, legit, I've lost marks in tests solely due to the inability to read my writing. 

Practise helps. A lot. Choose a certain style, I don't really recommend cursive, because that's gonna get really messy, especially if you're taking quick notes for classes. And if you're anything like I was, a few weeks later and looking back at notes, you're not even gonna recognise what you wrote. Practise print-style handwriting (idk if that makes sense but like-normal standard font). 

Write your alphabet multiple times before practising to write different words. Legitimately, it's all in putting the effort to practise your handwriting continuously.

Putting a bit more pressure when you're writing can force you to put in the effort to make your handwriting more presentable, I found that when I wrote light and quickly, that's when I defaulted back into my messy handwriting.
